text: It is sad to see a bakery after 40 years that just closed. I really dislike the fact that they just let these places close down. The owner is not crazy, rent went up, his equipment is very old, prices of his ingredients, of the flour, of the butter are very high. People order online, people buy cheaper bread from the supermarket. So yeah, maybe he is just retiring and that's OK. But at the same time, those bakeries are the heart of the city, the heart of the neighborhood. Grandparents and kids are standing in the same line, and everybody knows each other. People celebrate their birthdays in that bakery, the cake that they buy. They smell the yeast in the street, and that really makes the place alive. Those are the town square. And yeah, of course, it's not easy to maintain them. But you can't ask an elderly person to maintain them for a lifetime. It's about taking care of these places, making them sustainable. You need more policy, you need more patronage, you need maybe more forms of ownership to sustain these bakeries. You need to support them before they close.
